headline: Sterling is near 1.3217 against the dollar early on Tuesday in Dubai, inside the range of 1.3180 to 1.3250 it has kept since Friday, with the dollar steady just below Monday's 18-month high. High US bond yields and the euro's political troubles support the dollar, while Friday's weak US jobs figures and falling oil work against it, and the Fed minutes on Wednesday are the next scheduled test.

drivers.title: Fed rate expectations
drivers.text: Markets put the chance that the Fed leaves rates unchanged at its 28 October meeting at about 78%, Trading Economics reported on 6 October, after September's jobs report showed 29,000 jobs added against 90,000 expected. Traders still see a chance of more than 80% of a rise by the end of the year, FXStreet reported on 6 October. The minutes of the Fed's September meeting come out on Wednesday at 22:00 Dubai.

drivers.title: US bond yields
drivers.text: The US ten-year yield stood at 5.317% and the thirty-year at 5.677% late on Monday 5 October, Reuters reported, with long-term yields at their highest in more than two decades according to Trading Economics. Higher US yields draw money into the dollar. Prices paid by US services firms rose in September at the fastest pace since July 2022.

drivers.title: Oil supply
drivers.text: Brent closed Monday 5 October near $100.70 (about £76) a barrel. The G7 is releasing 100 million barrels of diesel and crude over four months, and JPMorgan estimates Middle East crude shipments at 17.5 million barrels a day, about 98% of the pre-war level, Trading Economics reported.

drivers.title: The Middle East
drivers.text: The US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz continues. The Houthis claimed three further missile and drone operations against airports, an oil facility and military sites in Saudi Arabia, FXStreet reported late on 5 October, and it also cited media reports that Israel is preparing possible military action against Iran, which other sources read for this update did not confirm.

drivers.title: France, Spain and the euro
drivers.text: The euro is near 1.1220 against the dollar, close to Monday's low, its weakest since May 2025, after falling 1.2% last week, Reuters reported on 5 October. Doubts over France's 2027 budget and the snap election called in Spain on 5 October lie behind it. A weaker euro lifts the dollar against other currencies, the pound included.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: The Bank of England held Bank Rate at 3.75% on 17 September, with three of the nine members voting for a rise, and its next decision is on 5 November. Markets price about 30 basis points of further tightening by the end of the year, Trading Economics reported on 2 October. No major UK figures are due this week.

lower: Fed minutes on Wednesday showing that most members want another rate rise, which would support the dollar.
US bond yields rising further from their highest levels in more than two decades, which draws money into the dollar.
The Saudi and Houthi fighting or the standoff with Iran cutting oil supply again, which tends to lift oil and the dollar.
The euro falling further on France's budget or Spain's election, which lifts the dollar against every currency.
higher: Fed minutes showing more doubt about further rises, which would add to the effect of Friday's weak jobs figures.
Oil falling further as the G7 release and recovering Gulf exports reach the market, which eases US inflation worries and weakens the dollar.
US weekly jobless claims on Thursday coming in above the 200,000 forecast, which would make Fed rises less likely.
watch: Nothing major is scheduled for Tuesday. The Fed minutes on Wednesday at 22:00 Dubai are the week's main event, and they carry no forecast: minutes showing more doubt about further rate rises would help someone selling pounds for dirhams, and minutes showing most members want another rise would work against them. US weekly jobless claims follow on Thursday at 16:30 Dubai, forecast at 200,000.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened as oil falls again
feed.text: Brent fell about 2% to near $98.30 (about £74) a barrel, its third fall in a row, as Saudi Arabia reported 5.8 million barrels flowing through its East-West Pipeline and Middle East exports recover, Trading Economics reported, and the dollar index slipped below 102 to about 101.87. Cheaper oil eases US inflation worries and the case for Fed rises, which weakens the dollar and means more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD rose from 1.3211 at 11:00 Dubai, as London opened, to 1.3243 at 13:00; the euro rose by a similar 0.3% and the pound was unchanged against the euro, so nothing in the UK lies behind it.

feed.title: Sterling has climbed above 1.3260 with no named cause
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from 1.3246 at 15:12 Dubai to 1.3266 at 15:30, above the range of 1.3180 to 1.3250 it had kept since Friday, and stood near 1.3262 at 15:39. The euro rose by a similar 0.15% against the dollar in those minutes and the pound was unchanged against the euro, so this is the dollar giving more ground rather than anything in the UK. No source names an event for those minutes, and no scheduled figure came out; BBH, quoted by FXStreet at 15:15 Dubai, said the dollar had trimmed its recent gains while futures still price a full Fed rise in December.

feed.title: Sterling has held just above 1.32 overnight
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from 1.3200 at 18:40 Dubai on Monday to 1.3224 by 19:00, then stayed between 1.3200 and 1.3227 through the US session and Tuesday's Asian trading, and stood near 1.3217 at 07:38 Dubai. The dollar index is steady near 102.16, just under Monday's 18-month high, and the euro is still near 1.1220, its weakest since May 2025, Reuters reported. No scheduled figure came out overnight, so the forces of Monday are unchanged: high US yields and the euro's troubles hold the dollar up, which means fewer dirhams per pound, while weak US jobs figures and cheaper oil hold it back.

feed.title: Oil has slipped as Gulf exports recover
feed.text: Brent closed Monday near $100.70 (about £76) a barrel and US crude fell to about $88.50 (about £67) early on Tuesday, Trading Economics and FXStreet reported, citing the G7 release and a JPMorgan estimate that Middle East crude shipments are back to about 98% of their pre-war level. Cheaper oil eases US inflation worries and tends to weaken the dollar, which would mean more dirhams per pound. Against that, the Houthis claimed three further missile and drone operations against airports, an oil facility and military sites in Saudi Arabia, and GBP/USD has barely moved, so the two have so far cancelled out.

feed.title: The US services survey was slightly soft, but prices rose
feed.text: The ISM services index for September came in at 54.9 against 55.1 forecast and 55.4 in August, Trading Economics reported, while its measure of prices paid rose to 74.0 from 72.6, the highest since July 2022, and its employment measure returned to growth at 50.1 from 47.8. A softer headline makes Fed rises a little less likely, which weakens the dollar, but faster price rises and firmer hiring point the other way, so the two largely cancelled out. GBP/USD rose from 1.3195 just before the release at 18:00 Dubai to 1.3202 four minutes later, touched 1.3205 at 18:12 and 1.3207 at 18:32, and stood near 1.3200 at 18:38.

feed.title: The dollar has strengthened as the euro hits a 17-month low
feed.text: Spain's prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, called a snap election today after Congress rejected his housing measures, which added to the worries over France's budget and took the euro to its weakest against the dollar since May 2025, Trading Economics and FXStreet reported. Money leaving the euro lifts the dollar against every currency, the pound included, which means fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD slid steadily from 1.3221 at 16:35 Dubai to 1.3192 at 17:38, with a low of 1.3191, while the euro fell by a similar 0.2% against the dollar and the pound was little changed against the euro, so nothing in the UK lies behind it; the US services survey follows at 18:00 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed again as the euro slips
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from 1.3230 at 13:38 Dubai to 1.3216 at 13:45 and has since held between about 1.3218 and 1.3225. The euro fell by the same 0.1% against the dollar in those minutes and the pound was unchanged against the euro, so this is the dollar strengthening, which means fewer dirhams per pound, and nothing in the UK. No source names a single event for those minutes; FXStreet, writing at 14:37 Dubai, put the dollar's strength down to heavy selling of the euro over France's budget, high long-term US yields and geopolitical tension, and Trading Economics added political uncertainty in Spain.

feed.title: The dollar has eased back from its morning high
feed.text: FXStreet put the dollar index near 102.53, a new high for the year, at about 10:00 Dubai, and Trading Economics showed it near 102.19 later in the morning, as London and Europe opened. Trading Economics also reported Brent slipping towards $101 (about £76) a barrel earlier in the session on signs of rising supply, which eases the pull of the dollar. GBP/USD has climbed steadily from about 1.3192 at 08:30 Dubai to about 1.3230 at 12:35 Dubai, recovering most of the early fall; the euro rose by about the same 0.3% over those hours, so this is the dollar giving ground, and no source names a single event for it.

feed.title: The dollar has strengthened in Asian trading
feed.text: FXStreet reported the dollar index above 102.20 just before 07:00 Dubai, citing higher US Treasury yields, the conflicts in the Middle East, worries about France's budget and remarks from the Fed's Lorie Logan that rates need to rise by at least a further 50 basis points. Money moving into the dollar for safety and for yield means fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD fell from 1.3233 at 06:00 Dubai to 1.3217 at 06:42 and a low of 1.3188 at 07:08, then recovered to about 1.3201 by 07:38; no source names a single event for the sharpest minutes. The euro fell further than the pound, about 0.5% against 0.3%, which points to the dollar and the euro, not to anything in the UK.

feed.title: The banks have reopened close to Friday's level
feed.text: GBP/USD was near 1.3245 an hour after the reopening at 01:00 Dubai, against 1.3237 at Friday's close. Kraken's weekend price had dipped to about 1.3211 on Sunday morning, and that dip has been reversed. Two pieces of weekend news pull in opposite directions, set out below.

feed.title: The G7 will release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude
feed.text: G7 leaders agreed on Friday to release the oil through the International Energy Agency over four months, with a large diesel release in the first 20 days, and diesel futures fell more than 4%. More supply lowers oil prices, which eases US inflation worries and tends to weaken the dollar, so each pound buys more dirhams.

feed.title: Fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis has intensified
feed.text: The Houthis claimed a missile and drone strike on an Aramco site south of Riyadh on Saturday, and Saudi and Yemeni forces have launched a counteroffensive. Threats to oil supply tend to lift oil and the dollar, which would mean fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: US jobs report for September
feed.text: Employers added 29,000 jobs against 90,000 expected, and July and August were revised down by a combined 60,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2% against 4.1% expected, and hourly pay rose 0.1% in the month against 0.3% expected. A cooling US job market and slower pay growth make another Fed rate rise less likely; Reuters reported that US two-year yields fell 7 basis points to 4.716% and ten-year yields 6 basis points to 5.176%, and the market chance of an October rise fell to as low as 12%, so the dollar weakened and GBP/USD rose. GBP/USD jumped from 1.3205 just before 16:30 Dubai to a high of 1.3250 in the first minute and 1.3236 two minutes later, slipped to about 1.3219 by 16:33, and has since moved between about 1.3212 and 1.3241. It was near 1.3226 at 17:40 Dubai, about 0.15% above its level before the report, taking GBP/AED from about 4.850 to about 4.857.

feed.title: Oil falls back below $100 (about £76)
feed.text: Trading Economics reported on Friday that Brent fell about 3% to around $99.30 (about £75.10), as European governments considered releasing strategic oil and fuel reserves to ease fuel costs and Middle East crude flows recovered towards pre-war levels. This reverses most of Thursday's jump on the carrier report. Cheaper oil eases inflation worries and the pull of the dollar as a safe haven, which tends to help the pound against the dollar, so each pound buys slightly more dirhams. The time of the move is not known. The fall in oil came on the same day as the weaker US jobs report, and GBP/USD stood about 0.3% above Thursday evening's low near 1.3183 by 17:40 Dubai.

feed.title: Dollar eases slightly in the European morning before the US jobs report
feed.text: FXStreet reported at about 11:15 Dubai that the dollar index had slipped back below 102.00 after reaching 102.20 on Thursday, its highest since April 2025, with GBP/USD slightly above 1.3210, up about 0.2% on the day. There was no UK data this morning, and FXStreet reported that the chance of an October Fed rise priced by markets had fallen to about 24%, from over 70% a week earlier. Traders tend to trim their dollar holdings before a big US report after a strong run, which lets the pound recover a little, so each pound buys slightly more dirhams. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3205 at 07:00 Dubai to a high near 1.3218 at about 10:30 Dubai, then settled near 1.3208 by 12:30 Dubai, taking GBP/AED from about 4.850 to about 4.854 and back to about 4.851.

feed.title: Oil steadies after Thursday's jump
feed.text: The National reported on Friday that Brent eased 0.05% to $102.10 (about £77.30) and US crude 0.31% to $92.58 (about £70.10), as larger Saudi shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, 2.9 million barrels a day in September against about 1 million in August, balanced the US carrier deployment. OPEC+ meets on Sunday to set November output. Steady oil removes one source of fresh demand for the dollar, though prices above $100 (about £76) keep inflation worries and US yields high. The time of the news is not known. Oil's pause matched a quiet morning for GBP/USD, which stayed between about 1.3200 and 1.3218.

feed.title: Sterling near its lowest since June in Asian trading
feed.text: FXStreet reported GBP/USD below 1.3200 in Asian trading on Friday, near its lowest since 26 June, with the dollar index near 102, its highest since spring 2025, and traders waiting for the US jobs report. Brent rose a further 0.3% to $102.60 (about £77.70), Reuters reported. With US yields high and oil dear, money has kept flowing into the dollar, so each pound buys fewer dirhams; quiet trading before a big report tends to hold the rate near its lows. GBP/USD eased from about 1.3195 at 03:30 Dubai to a low near 1.3180 at about 05:35 Dubai, then recovered to about 1.3204 by 07:35 Dubai, taking GBP/AED from about 4.840 back to about 4.849.

feed.title: Report of a third US aircraft carrier for the Middle East lifts oil
feed.text: The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday that the US is sending the USS Theodore Roosevelt strike group to the Middle East, with up to 10,000 more troops, and a US official confirmed the deployment to The National. Brent for December settled up 4.4% at $102.31 (about £77.50) and US crude up 2.7% at $92.87 (about £70.40). Dearer oil and the risk of renewed conflict with Iran push up inflation worries and US yields and draw money into the dollar as a safe haven, so each pound buys fewer dirhams. The time of the report is not known. GBP/USD slid from about 1.3226 at 18:45 Dubai to about 1.3207 at 19:05 Dubai and to a low near 1.3183 by 19:50 Dubai, then settled near 1.3190 through the evening.

feed.title: US factory survey (ISM), September
feed.text: 54.5 against 55.0 expected and 54.6 in August, the ninth month of growth in a row. The prices paid index jumped to 77.9 from 71.1, and the employment index rose to 52.7 from 51.2. A slightly softer headline would normally weaken the dollar, but the sharp rise in prices paid points to more inflation, which keeps a Fed rise in play and supported the dollar. GBP/USD fell from 1.3234 just before the release to about 1.3221 within five minutes, then held near 1.3225 for the next half hour.

feed.title: UK 30-year borrowing costs pass 6% for the first time since 1998
feed.text: The 30-year gilt yield briefly reached about 6.03% on Thursday and the 10-year gilt yield moved above 5.50%, its highest since 2007, amid worries about energy-driven inflation, heavy government borrowing and the Budget on 28 October. The FTSE 100 lost 177.73 points. When UK yields rise because investors worry about the public finances, rather than because the economy is strong, the pound tends to fall with gilt prices, so each pound buys fewer dirhams. This weighed on sterling through Thursday alongside the firmer dollar; GBP/USD fell from about 1.3263 early on Thursday to about 1.3190 by the evening.

feed.title: US weekly jobless claims
feed.text: 197,000 new claims in the week to 26 September, against about 201,000 expected, the lowest since July. Continuing claims fell to 1.701 million. Fewer people losing their jobs points to a strong US labour market, which normally keeps a Fed rise in play and supports the dollar. GBP/USD edged up from 1.3228 just before the release to about 1.3235 within two minutes, as sterling had already fallen a long way that morning.
